nodes.author: ACSEngSafety
nodes.text:
Fed the results to an AI for a plain language summary:
"Here’s a plain language summary of the study:

The researchers compared the vaccination status of two groups of people: 2880 people who had non-influenza respiratory viruses and 3240 people who tested negative for any viruses. They found that being vaccinated didn’t significantly change the likelihood of getting non-influenza respiratory viruses compared to not being vaccinated. Specifically, the odds ratio was 0.97, meaning vaccinated people were almost just as likely to get these viruses as non-vaccinated people.

They also looked at the vaccination status of 3349 people who had influenza and compared them to three different groups: all the control subjects (total 6120), those who tested positive for non-influenza viruses (2880 people), and those who tested negative for all viruses (3240 people). The odds ratios for these comparisons ranged from 0.46 to 0.51, indicating that vaccinated people were less likely to have influenza compared to these control groups.

Essentially, the study suggests that vaccination doesn’t significantly reduce the risk for non-influenza respiratory viruses, but it does lower the risk of getting influenza."
https://t.co/rJnEV9y58e
